title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 8

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Why will heating be switched off in the old laboratory?
tasks.audioText: The facilities team will switch off heating in the old laboratory during the spring break while maintenance is carried out. Students who need access to stored equipment should contact the technician before Friday. The team is also testing motion sensors in two corridors. Feedback about lighting levels can be sent through the maintenance form on the college portal.
options: Because maintenance is being carried out
Because the laboratory is being repainted
Because new computers are being installed
Because maintenance is being carried out

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. How can students send feedback about corridor lighting?
tasks.audioText: The facilities team will switch off heating in the old laboratory during the spring break while maintenance is carried out. Students who need access to stored equipment should contact the technician before Friday. The team is also testing motion sensors in two corridors. Feedback about lighting levels can be sent through the maintenance form on the college portal.
options: On Friday
Through the maintenance form on the college portal
Next month
After the event

tasks.prompt: An energy audit at a college found that several computer rooms remained fully lit after the last lesson. The facilities team introduced a simple closing checklist and asked the final group to check lights and equipment. The audit also recommended replacing older lamps with more efficient models. After a month, electricity use had decreased, although the team planned to compare figures over a longer period. Reading 1. What problem did the audit identify?
options: The laboratory heating was left on overnight
Computer rooms stayed fully lit after the last lesson
Computer rooms stayed fully lit after the last lesson
Students left windows open during lessons
A timetable for switching off computers
A closing checklist for the final group
A new system for booking laboratories
A closing checklist for the final group

tasks.prompt: The equipment should ___ before the room is locked.
options: be switched off
switch off
be switching
switched off by students yesterday

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO practical ways to reduce electricity use at college.
options: Leave computers running overnight without a reason
Ignore maintenance problems
Switch off unused lights and equipment
Use energy-efficient lighting

tasks.prompt: The amount of energy used by a building is its energy ___.
You are writing to the facilities team about an energy-saving idea. Which sentence is best?
options: You must install my idea immediately.
Would it be possible to test motion sensors in another corridor?
Your energy policy makes no sense.
I will change the lighting myself.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of saving energy at college in a logical order.
options: Test the improvement and record usage
Identify where energy is being wasted
Review the results over time
Suggest a suitable improvement
correctOrder: Identify where energy is being wasted
Test the improvement and record usage

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words proposing one way your college could save energy. Explain how it could be introduced and how its effect could be measured.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: one practical college energy-saving measure is proposed (0–2); the response explains how it could be introduced and how its effect could be measured (0–2); the proposal is clearly sequenced with understandable grammar (0–2); energy/measurement vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
